:::{#thm-null-gram}
#### $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}$ has the same null space as $\matr{A}$

For any $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$,

$$
\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}) = \mathcal{N}(\matr{A}).
$$

:::

::: proof

**$\mathcal{N}(\matr{A}) \subseteq \mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A})$.**
If $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$,
then $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \tp{\matr{A}}\,\vzero_m = \vzero_n$.

**$\mathcal{N}(\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}) \subseteq \mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$.**
If $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_n$, then

$$
\ba
0
&= \tp{\vecf{x}}\,\vzero_n
&& \text{(every term of the inner product is } 0 \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{x}}\,\paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x}}
&& \text{(substitute } \vzero_n = \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x} \text{)}
\\
&= \paren{\tp{\vecf{x}} \tp{\matr{A}}}\,(\matr{A} \vecf{x})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \tp{(\matr{A} \vecf{x})}\,(\matr{A} \vecf{x})
&& \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
\\
&= (\matr{A} \vecf{x}) \cdot (\matr{A} \vecf{x})
&& \text{(@exm-dot-product-matmul)}
\\
&= \norm{\matr{A} \vecf{x}}^2.
&& \text{(square both sides of @eq-l2-norm)}
\ea
$$

A vector whose Euclidean norm is $0$ has every entry $0$,
so $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_m$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-null-gram}
#### The null space of a Gram matrix

For $\matr{A}$ in @exm-column-space,

$$
\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 \\ -2 & -6 \end{bmatrix}
  \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & -6 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 10 & -20 & -20 \\ -20 & 40 & 40 \\ -20 & 40 & 40 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Every row is a multiple of $(1, -2, -2)$,
so $\tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vzero_3$
exactly when $x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3 = 0$,
the same condition as for $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$ in @exm-null-space.

:::
